categories.main_business_segments: As of 2022, Zillow Group operated three main business segments: Internet, Media & Technology (IMT), Mortgages, and Homes. The IMT segment includes Premier Agent and rentals marketplaces, as well as other advertising and business technology solutions for real estate professionals. The Mortgages segment covers mortgage originations through Zillow Home Loans and advertising sold to mortgage lenders and professionals. The Homes segment primarily includes title and escrow services via Zillow Closing Services, with the iBuying business (Zillow Offers) wound down and presented as discontinued operations.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Zillow's core technologies center on its proprietary data aggregation and analytics platform, including the patented Zestimate automated valuation model, which leverages advanced algorithms and a living database of approximately 140 million U.S. homes. The company invests heavily in software development, cloud infrastructure, and machine learning to power its consumer-facing platforms, transaction management tools, and mortgage origination systems. Technology solutions such as ShowingTime+, dotloop, and Bridge Interactive support real estate professionals with scheduling, transaction management, and interactive floor plans.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Zillow primarily serves home buyers, sellers, renters, and real estate professionals (agents, brokers, property managers, and mortgage lenders) in the U.S. residential real estate market. Its platforms connect consumers with agents (Premier Agent), rental listings, mortgage products, and transaction services, while also providing advertising and technology solutions to industry partners. The company also targets home builders and landlords through its new construction and rentals marketplaces.
categories.geographic_coverage: Zillow operates nationwide in the United States, with its core platforms and services available across all 50 states and the District of Columbia. Zillow Home Loans is licensed in 48 states and D.C., and the company has a limited presence in Canada and some operations in Serbia for workforce purposes. Major office locations include Seattle, San Francisco, New York, Atlanta, Irvine, Denver, and Overland Park.
categories.supply_chain_position: Zillow operates primarily as a downstream, technology-enabled marketplace and service provider, connecting end consumers with real estate professionals and facilitating residential real estate transactions. Through Zillow Home Loans and Zillow Closing Services, it also participates in mortgage origination and title/escrow services, but does not own or develop physical real estate assets following the wind-down of its iBuying business.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Zillow's strategic focus is on building a 'housing super app' that integrates all aspects of the real estate transaction, aiming to increase customer transactions and revenue per transaction. Key R&D initiatives include enhancing touring experiences, expanding financing and seller services, strengthening the partner network, and integrating services for seamless customer journeys. The company emphasizes innovation in data science, automation, and digital transaction management, with significant investment in technology and product development.
categories.revenue_model: Zillow generates revenue primarily through advertising and marketing services sold to real estate professionals (notably Premier Agent), rental and new construction listings, and business technology solutions. Additional revenue streams include mortgage origination and resale (Zillow Home Loans), title and escrow services (Zillow Closing Services), and software-as-a-service subscriptions (e.g., dotloop, ShowingTime+). The company employs both subscription and performance-based (pay-for-performance) pricing models.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Zillow faces competition from a fragmented landscape of traditional real estate brokerages, rental listing services, mortgage lenders, and technology-driven real estate platforms. Major online competitors include Realtor.com, Redfin, CoStar (apartments.com), and Opendoor, as well as local brokerages and MLSs. Zillow is the most visited real estate website in the U.S. and is widely recognized as the leading online residential real estate brand, but holds a small share of total U.S. real estate and mortgage transactions.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2022, Zillow reported $2.0 billion in revenue (down 8% from 2021), with a net loss of $101 million from continuing operations. The company maintains a strong liquidity position with $3.4 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and investments, and $1.7 billion in convertible debt. While the company experienced contraction in mortgage and Premier Agent revenues due to macroeconomic headwinds, it remains one of the largest digital real estate platforms in the U.S. and continues to invest in growth and technology.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Zillow's value proposition centers on providing the most comprehensive, trusted, and user-friendly digital real estate experience, powered by its proprietary data, the Zestimate, and a vast living database of U.S. homes. The company differentiates itself through brand recognition, technology leadership, integrated transaction services, and a large, engaged consumer audience. Its platform aims to make real estate transactions faster, easier, and more transparent for both consumers and industry partners.
